name: Should I Repair or Replace My Roof in Los Angeles County?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my Los Angeles County roof needs repair or full replacement after a leak?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if my Los Angeles County roof needs repair or full replacement after a leak?

acceptedAnswer.text: The fastest way to decide between repair and replacement is to look at the age of the roof, the number of leak points, and whether damage is localized or widespread. A small flashing failure or a few missing shingles can often be repaired. If water intrusion has spread into the decking, multiple roof planes, or the same area keeps failing, replacement may be the better investment. In Los Angeles County, sun exposure, heat cycling, and occasional storms can make older roofs fail unevenly, so two roofs of the same age may not perform the same way. A proper inspection should include the attic, decking, underlayment, penetrations, and drainage paths. If you are comparing bids, ask contractors to separate emergency repairs, long-term repairs, and full replacement pricing so you can see the cost difference clearly. The best choice is usually the one that stops the leak reliably and avoids repeated service calls.
acceptedAnswer.description: A roof usually needs repair if the leak is isolated, the structure is sound, and damage is limited to a small area. Replacement is more likely when leaks are recurring, shingles or membrane sections are widespread, or the roof is near the end of its service life. A professional inspection should check decking, flashing, underlayment, and ventilation.
